Using \(\tan(3\pi-x)=\tan(\pi-x)=-\tan x\), we get
\[
-\tan x=2 \implies \tan x=-2.
\]
Now
\[
2\cos^2\frac{x}{2}-1=\cos x,
\]
so
\[
\frac{2\cos^2\frac{x}{2}-\sin x-1}{\sin x+\cos x}
=
\frac{\cos x-\sin x}{\sin x+\cos x}.
\]
Divide numerator and denominator by \(\cos x\):
\[
\frac{1-\tan x}{\tan x+1}
=
\frac{1-(-2)}{-2+1}
=
\frac{3}{-1}
=
-3.
\]
\[
\boxed{-3}
\]
